newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia net foreign reserves $9.48 bln at end '96.
newsitem.headline: Colombia net foreign reserves $9.48 bln at end '96.

text.p: Colombia's net foreign reserves stood at $9.48 billion as of December 27, the last working day of 1996, the central bank said in a report Monday.
The figure represents a 13.8 percent increase, $1.16 billion, compared to net foreign reserves reported on the last day of 1995, according to the bank's report.
The central bank had forecast net foreign reserves to rise by just $100 million through 1996.

The much larger than expected rise was due to the strengthening peso, which obliged the central bank to step in and prop up the dollar, and also dollar payments for three newly-privatized power generators, which the government sold in December.
In the December 20-27 period, net reserves rose by $543.2 million and between November 30 and December 20 increased by $560 million.

The unexpected rise in the net foreign reserves in December -- more than the total increase forecast for 1997 -- will now force the government to re-think some of its economic targets, particularly interest rate, exchange rate and public debt policies, Juan Carlos Ramirez, head of the National Planning Department said Monday.
